items.body_html: entering a human_gate sets WAITING(human_decision) AND records DECISION_REQUEST atomically; a failed append rolls back — no externally valid half-entered gate (we do not bind to a write order)

a KICKOFF sibling guarded by wait.kind + request correlation + operator authority + op_id + CAS; operator authority is checked here, the full operator authority model is later — the L1 actor gate is a different input class
no agent is dispatched while parked on a human decision; the human is the only mover until the decision resumes the instance

a decision against the recorded recommendation (chosen ≠ recommended) requires override: true, written into DECISION_MADE — the fiduciary core. Override is meaningful only against a recommendation: with none recorded, or when agreeing with it, an override is override_not_applicable

a decision whose target advances_round (a loop-back, e.g. rework → implement) clears the stale review/decision context and opens a new round — keyed on round advancement, not on a verdict name; the fresh decision payload stays as the handoff

items.name_html: a decision carries its required payload
items.body_html: a decision's required payload fields are declared per decision in the gate's decisions map (anchor: request_rework ⇒ instruction required, + optional refs) — a missing one is missing_required_field (the generic replacement for the old hardcoded rework rule); the payload is recorded in DECISION_MADE and delivered actor-facing as the handoff of the target’s first dispatch. approve declares none

a decision routes to decisions[verdict].target; the target's type decides arrival (agent ⇒ ACTIVE, type: human_gate ⇒ park human_decision, type: wait ⇒ park WAITING(step.wait.kind), terminal ⇒ COMPLETE), via the one apply_target_entry_effects(...) HANDLE and SUBMIT_DECISION share. So approve can target another gate, an agent step (even a newly-added LLM step), a wait step, or done — there is no privileged "finalization" phase and the kernel never bakes in "approve = finalize"; the kernel knows no decision names. An undeclared key is unknown_decision; the L0d closed terminal set done | failed | cancelled is untouched

items.name_html: a parked wait resumes only on a matching event
items.body_html: a WAITING instance moves forward only via RESUME_WAIT on an event whose type is in wait.resume_events, routed by the step's on_resume — guarded by idempotency (op_id) + version (CAS), like HANDLE; an unrouted resume is no_resume_transition. KICKOFF and SUBMIT_DECISION are the specialized resumes (activation / decision); RESUME_WAIT is the bare one. The resume action (e.g. running git commit) is not the kernel's job here
